headline: The swap that changed target
rationale_specialist: The anilino methanesulfonamide of the hit was replaced by an sp3 1-(methylsulfonyl)piperidin-4-ylamine at the pyrimidine C2 position. Precedent in this hinge region (ebvaciclib against zotiraciclib, and an aminopiperidine analogue of milciclib) associates sp3 hybridisation here with general kinase selectivity, and that is how the authors rationalise the result.
rationale_plain: The starting molecule was really a JAK2 inhibitor. Replacing its flat aniline with a puckered, three-dimensional ring stopped it hitting JAK2 at all, and made it 38 times better at CDK2.

headline: Chlorine to trifluoromethyl at the gatekeeper
rationale_specialist: Exchanging the C5 chloro for a trifluoromethyl fills the space against the Phe80 gatekeeper. CDK2 potency improved five-fold and CDK1 selectivity went from 64-fold to 130-fold, which established C5 as the isoform selectivity lever for the whole series.
rationale_plain: A small chlorine atom was swapped for a bulkier fluorinated group, right where the protein has a bulky residue of its own. This is the single change that separated CDK2 from its dangerous relative CDK1.

headline: Tetrahydropyran to cyclohexyl
rationale_specialist: Replacing the tetrahydropyran oxygen with a plain methylene gives a lipophilic cyclohexyl. Potency and CDK1 selectivity survive, but simulated gastric fluid solubility falls to 11 ug/mL and human microsomal clearance rises to 1.1 L/h/kg.
rationale_plain: Removing a single oxygen atom made the molecule greasier. It still worked on the enzyme, but it dissolved poorly and the liver cleared it quickly.

headline: Isoelectronic swap to N-methylpiperidine
rationale_specialist: The cyclohexyl is exchanged for an isoelectronic 1-methylpiperidin-4-yl. Solubility clears 400 ug/mL and clearance falls to 0.7 L/h/kg, but CDK1 selectivity collapses from 130-fold to 29-fold and CDK6 potency drops to 153 nM.
rationale_plain: Putting a nitrogen into the ring fixed the solubility problem immediately. The cost was severe: the molecule lost most of its margin over CDK1.

headline: Saturated ring to ortho-fluorophenyl
rationale_specialist: Moving from a saturated ring to an ortho-fluorophenyl is tolerated in the enzyme assay at 2.1 nM with 170-fold CDK1 selectivity and clearance below 0.5 L/h/kg, but whole blood potency is poor at about 5 uM.
rationale_plain: An aromatic ring worked just as well against the purified enzyme, and the liver left it alone. In human blood, though, it barely worked at all: a warning that enzyme numbers are not the whole story.

headline: Fluorine to chlorine
rationale_specialist: The ortho-fluorine becomes an ortho-chlorine. Enzyme potency improves nearly four-fold to 0.56 nM and whole blood potency improves six-fold to 823 nM, but human intrinsic clearance rises to 1 L/h/kg.
rationale_plain: Swapping fluorine for the larger chlorine made the molecule work far better in blood. The liver then cleared it faster, which is the problem the next few compounds try to solve.

headline: Ring to 2,2,2-trifluoroethyl
rationale_specialist: Dropping the ring entirely for a short fluorinated chain keeps potency at 1.8 nM with 110-fold CDK1 selectivity and clearance below 0.5 L/h/kg, but solubility is only 3 ug/mL.
rationale_plain: Replacing the ring with a small fluorinated tail kept the potency and the liver stability. It would barely dissolve, which is what the sulfonyl end of the molecule was then used to fix.

headline: Fluorinated tail to geminal dimethyl alcohol
rationale_specialist: Exchanging the trifluoroethyl for a 2-hydroxy-2-methylpropyl group gives subnanomolar potency at 0.42 nM, 150-fold CDK1 selectivity, solubility of 842 ug/mL and clearance below 0.5 L/h/kg, at the cost of CDK6 potency at 160 nM.
rationale_plain: Adding an alcohol group made the compound dissolve nearly three hundred times better and pushed potency below one nanomolar. This is the branch that eventually produced the lead.

headline: A nitrile to slow the liver down
rationale_specialist: A cyano group at the para position of the 2-chlorophenyl lowers lipophilicity to cut intrinsic clearance to 0.5 L/h/kg while holding potency at 0.3 nM, but gastric solubility falls below 1 ug/mL.
rationale_plain: Adding a small polar group stopped the liver clearing the compound so fast. Solubility got worse again: the two properties kept trading against each other.

headline: An ionisable amine for solubility
rationale_specialist: The nitrile becomes an N-methyl benzylamine, which both breaks molecular planarity and adds an ionisable centre. Solubility rises to 94 ug/mL, but CDK1 selectivity falls to 81-fold and CDK7 to 62-fold.
rationale_plain: A basic amine was added to help the compound dissolve, and it did. But it also narrowed the safety margin over CDK1 and CDK7.

headline: Trifluoromethyl to nitrile
rationale_specialist: Returning to the C5 lever, the trifluoromethyl is replaced by a cyano group. CDK1 selectivity recovers to 290-fold, CDK7 to 790-fold, and solubility improves to 221 ug/mL. Free fraction rises to 33%, which is how the authors explain the good whole blood translation at 112 nM.
rationale_plain: Changing that one group again recovered the lost safety margins and improved solubility at the same time. It also made more of the drug available in blood rather than stuck to blood proteins.

headline: Methyl sulfonyl to N-methylpyrazole
rationale_specialist: The methyl on the sulfonyl is replaced by a 1-methylpyrazol-4-yl. Potency, clearance and Caco-2 permeability are all good, but gastric solubility stays below 1 ug/mL, so the solubility problem is not at this position yet.
rationale_plain: Putting a small ring on the sulfonyl end kept everything good except the one thing they were trying to fix. The compound still would not dissolve.

headline: The nitrogen walk that fixed solubility
rationale_specialist: Moving one ring nitrogen, from 1-methylpyrazol-4-yl to the more polar 1-methylimidazol-4-yl, raises gastric solubility from below 1 ug/mL to 322 ug/mL while holding the ADME profile and improving whole blood potency to 334 nM.
rationale_plain: Moving a single nitrogen atom around the ring made the compound over three hundred times more soluble. Nothing else about it got worse. This is the cleanest single edit in the paper.

headline: The C5 lever does not always help
rationale_specialist: Applying the C5 trifluoromethyl to nitrile change that worked for 12 improves CDK1 selectivity to 290-fold and CDK7 to 5600-fold, but solubility falls from 322 to 5 ug/mL, CDK4 and CDK6 margins narrow, and Caco-2 permeability drops to 0.6.
rationale_plain: The same trick that helped earlier backfired here: selectivity improved but the compound stopped dissolving and stopped crossing membranes. Context, not the group itself, decides the outcome.

headline: Imidazole to 2-pyridyl
rationale_specialist: Swapping the methylimidazole for a 2-pyridyl restores Caco-2 permeability to 18 but drops gastric solubility below 1 ug/mL. The authors record this as the point at which balancing the two at R3 was abandoned for this series.
rationale_plain: Another ring swap traded solubility straight back for permeability. After this the chemists gave up on this branch and went back to compound 9.

headline: The cyclopropyl that finished it
rationale_specialist: With the pyrazole alcohol of 9 fixed, a cyclopropyl on the sulfonyl gives 0.29 nM potency, 220-fold CDK1 selectivity, gastric solubility above 400 ug/mL, clearance of 0.5 L/h/kg and Caco-2 of 13. This is compound 17, the lead, and the ligand in 8UV0.
rationale_plain: A small three-carbon ring on the sulfonyl end was the last piece. Everything the chemists wanted was finally true at once, and this is the molecule they took forward.

headline: The C5 lever fails a third time
rationale_specialist: Applying the nitrile once more halves potency to 0.65 nM and narrows CDK1 to 190-fold, CDK4 to 26-fold and CDK6 to 95-fold, with solubility down to 41 ug/mL. On this scaffold the trifluoromethyl is the better group, which closes the C5 question the campaign opened at compound 2.
rationale_plain: Trying the same swap on the finished molecule made it worse in every way that mattered. The trifluoromethyl stayed.
